lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Here it is: your own garage. One service bay for working on cars, parking for keeping them, the day and your cash up in the top corner, and the labour bar down by the End Day button: your working day. Spanner work drains it; a night's sleep (press End Day) refills it.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: The tabs along the top are your world: the office phone where work finds you, the auction rooms, the parts shop. We will visit each one when it matters.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Start on the Phone tab: the shop's office phone. Customers ring with work, and the odd one walks straight in. Yuki is the walk-in kind: a student who has been saving all year and needs four wheels that will pass inspection. She has {payout}.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: She will hand you the whole envelope and trust you with it. Build her something roadworthy for less, and whatever is left over is your pay: every job in this trade works like that.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Accept the job when you are ready.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Now the Auctions tab. There are several auction rooms in town, but a young garage starts in one: {venue}. Cheap cars and quick hammers, and exactly the right hunting ground for Yuki's budget.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: The permit behind the till covers any auction house in town. Getting through their doors is another matter: the bigger rooms want a member to vouch for you.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: There is a {model} on the block that could be just right for her. Nothing glamorous, but read her sheet: she runs hot in traffic. The room can only price that at the odds, and the odds on a hot engine run from a morning's work to a scrapped car. Prove which it is and you know something the price does not.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Only one way to find out. Press Inspect here: a small fee and a little labour buys us an hour in the yard with the cars. Grab a coffee from the vending machine on the way in; the truth is worth more than the fee.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Cheapest test first. Cap off the header tank, run her up to temperature and watch the water. If combustion is getting past into the coolant you will see it come up as bubbles. Ten minutes.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Bubbles, steady as you like. That is combustion pushing into the water, and it is one of two things: a head gasket on its way out, or a crack in the block itself. One is a day with the head off. The other is a scrapped engine and a wasted trip. Compression test, and let us find out which.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Even compression across every pot, and the oil clean on the stick. Not the block, then: a head gasket on its way out and nothing worse. A day's work and a gasket set. The room heard a hot engine and priced it like scrap, and their fear is our discount.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Take a seat. It's a quiet morning and nobody else came for her: bid the reserve, the least the seller will take, and let the clock run out. Winning slowly still counts as winning.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.text: Oh, that one! I know she's had a hard life, but look at her. There's a good little car under all those miles, I can feel it from here.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: The {model} is yours, and she is sitting in parking looking sorry for herself. Tools only reach a car in the service bay: drag her across (or open her and press Move to service bay) and let us get a proper look.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Open her from the bay. She comes up in three views: the Body, the Engine bay, and the Underside, which is her up on the lift. Click anything and the panel below shows what you can do to it. Wheels live underneath, so switch to Underside and click hers.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Start at the ground. Her tyres are scrap, and scrap tyres fail a roadworthy all on their own. Tyres come off with the wheels: press Remove assembly (an assembly costs the same labour as pulling its parts one at a time, and the figure is on the button), and the wheels land on the bench below.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Fresh tyres, then. In the Parts tab, open Wheels & tyres and pick Tyres. Set the fits this vehicle dropdown to her {model} and the shop shows only what fits her; press Add to cart on the plain stock tyres. Sport rubber is lovely, and entirely not in her budget.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: In the cart, tick Express delivery and press Checkout to place the order. Standard lands tomorrow morning; express costs a surcharge but she gets her car today. That surcharge is usually the price of planning badly; today it's the price of not making Yuki wait on my timetable.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Tyres ordered. Nothing more we can do tonight, and that is fine: press End Day, and they will be on the shelf with the morning.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: There they are: four fresh tyres. Pressing them onto rims is machine work, and we do not own the machine yet: under Machine hire, take the Tyre machine & balancer for the day. One price, and it presses everything you bring it until closing; one day we will buy our own and stop renting. Then click the Tyres block on the bench, press Take it off to clear the scrap ones, then press Fit and pick the fresh stock tyres from the warehouse.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Fresh rubber on. Press Refit assembly and the wheels go back on, better than she has had in years.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: That gasket is what will fail her inspection. Switch to the Engine bay view and click the {part}. The panel underneath prices three jobs side by side: a Service takes her to worn, a Rebuild to fine, a Restore to mint. Read the figures before you touch anything. She only needs the first.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Press Service and the trolley rolls in carrying exactly the tools this job wants. Tap the one that is lit, and only the one that is lit: each tap works a step, tells you what you just did, and takes its bite out of the day. Two steps and the gasket is behind us.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.text: Careful with that! Sorry. I'll stop watching. ...I won't, though.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Look at what that first step cost against the second. The head sits buried under everything else, and reaching it is awkward work whoever is doing it, so the first step of a job done in the car pays for the reach. A part you have taken out and set on a bench never does, and that is what the benches are for: a Rebuild or a Restore wants the part off the car and over on the right one, with a better toolbox than ours.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: She goes back to her owner whole or not at all: every slot filled, nothing of hers left on a shelf. If anything is still in the warehouse, click its empty slot, press Fit and pick it. Putting back exactly what came off costs nothing.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: Back to the Phone tab. Pick the {model} on her card and press Show them the car; she will look it over, and when every line reads green, press Hand it over. Go on: she has waited long enough.

lines.speaker: instruction
lines.text: That is the walkthrough done, and your first happy customer on the road. From here it is yours to run. The phone rings most mornings with work you can take or leave. When you want a car of your own to fix and sell on, the local yard is the cheap end of the market and it is where everyone starts. And keep half an eye on what the week costs: hired tools and rushed parts come out of the till whether a car pays or not. The day you would rather own the crane than keep hiring it is the day the shop starts working for you.
